title: India-UK Free Trade Agreement Comes into Force on July 15, 2026
summary: The India-United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement (FTA), described as the 'most ambitious and aspirational' FTA India has ever concluded, entered into force on July 15, 2026. The deal is expected to boost Indian exports, reduce tariffs on goods such as Scotch whisky and automobiles, and benefit Indian professionals and businesses in the UK. It covers goods, services, investments, and intellectual property, making it one of the most comprehensive bilateral trade pacts India has signed.
exam_angle: India's FTA architecture and trade diplomacy are key GS-2 topics; this is India's most significant FTA with a developed economy and will be a benchmark case for trade policy questions.
key_facts: Effective date: July 15, 2026
Described as India's 'most ambitious and aspirational' FTA
Covers goods, services, investment, and IP
Key benefits: reduced tariffs on Indian textiles/seafood; cheaper UK whisky and cars in India

title: India Bans Import of Goods Produced Using Forced Labour
summary: India has notified a ban on the import of goods produced through the use of forced labour, amending its customs/foreign trade rules. The move comes even as a US Section 301 investigation into India's trade practices is pending. The notification aligns India with international labour standards and is seen as a pre-emptive measure to strengthen India's position in global trade negotiations, particularly with the US.
exam_angle: Links to India's Customs Act, Foreign Trade Policy, and international labour standards (ILO conventions); relevant for GS-2 governance and GS-3 economy questions on trade policy.
key_facts: India bans import of goods made using forced labour via customs notification
Move comes amid pending US Section 301 trade investigation against India
Aligns India with ILO Convention on forced labour
Relevant legislation: Customs Act / Foreign Trade (Development & Regulation) Act

title: India Launches UNSC Campaign for 2028-29 Term; Jaishankar Unveils 'SHANTI' Vision
summary: India has formally launched its campaign for a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) for the 2028-29 term. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar unveiled India's guiding vision framework called 'SHANTI' (an acronym representing India's five-point agenda for the UNSC). India previously held a non-permanent seat in 2021-22 and has been a strong advocate for UNSC reform to include permanent representation for developing nations.
exam_angle: UNSC membership, India's multilateral diplomacy, and UNSC reform are recurring GS-2 topics; the 'SHANTI' acronym and India's campaign priorities are memorisable facts.
key_facts: India campaigning for UNSC non-permanent seat for term 2028-29
EAM Jaishankar unveiled 'SHANTI' vision framework
India's previous UNSC non-permanent seat: 2021-22
UNSC has 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms

title: India Summons Iranian Envoy After Indian Sailor Killed in Hormuz Ship Strike
summary: India summoned the Iranian Ambassador to formally protest after Iranian missiles struck UAE-flagged tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, killing at least one Indian crew member and injuring others. The MEA stated that both attacked vessels carried 30 Indian seafarers, and India condemned the attacks 'in the strongest terms.' Approximately 148 Indian seafarers are reported to be in the Strait of Hormuz region amid the escalating US-Iran conflict.
exam_angle: India's diaspora protection, the MEA's consular obligations, and the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz (through which ~20% of global oil trade passes) are key exam points.
key_facts: Iran summoned by India's MEA over Hormuz ship attack
At least 1 Indian sailor killed; both vessels carried 30 Indian seafarers
~148 Indian seafarers reported in Hormuz region
Strait of Hormuz: critical chokepoint for global oil supply (~20% of world oil)

title: US-Iran Military Conflict Escalates: Airstrikes, Hormuz Blockade and Oil Price Surge
summary: The US launched fresh airstrikes on Iran, with President Trump claiming Iran 'shot first.' Iran warned of retaliation and signalled it could extend disruptions to the Red Sea. Trump also withdrew a previously threatened 20% levy on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, instead calling for trade deals with Gulf countries. The escalation sent crude oil prices to a one-month high, with Brent crude surging, and caused India's Sensex to fall ~560 points.
exam_angle: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical energy chokepoint directly affecting India's oil import bill, rupee, and inflation; this also tests knowledge of West Asia geopolitics, US-Iran relations, and India's energy security.
key_facts: US launched airstrikes on Iran; Trump claims Iran 'shot first'
Trump withdrew proposed 20% levy on ships through Strait of Hormuz
Crude oil surged to one-month high on conflict escalation
Sensex fell ~560 points; Rupee fell 62 paise to 96.30 vs USD

title: Trump Backs Russia Sanctions Bill That Could Impose 500% Tariffs on India
summary: US President Donald Trump has backed a Congressional bill proposing 500% tariffs on countries that continue to trade with Russia using Russian oil, a measure that directly threatens India. India is one of the largest buyers of discounted Russian crude oil since the 2022 Ukraine conflict. The bill, if enacted, would force India into a difficult choice between its energy security interests and its relationship with the United States.
exam_angle: India-Russia-US triangular relations, India's energy security (dependence on Russian crude), and secondary sanctions are important IR topics frequently tested in UPSC Mains.
key_facts: Proposed US bill: 500% tariffs on countries trading with Russia
India is among the largest buyers of Russian crude oil post-2022
Trump has backed the bill; passage would severely impact India's oil imports
Links to India's balancing act between US and Russia partnerships

title: Bharat Tex 2026: India's Largest Global Textile Event Inaugurated with Record International Participation
summary: Union Minister of Textiles inaugurated Bharat Tex 2026, described as India's largest global textile and apparel trade event. The event recorded the highest-ever international participation, reflecting India's ambition to position itself as a global textile hub. Bharat Tex 2026 comes at a time when the India-UK FTA has just entered into force, opening new export avenues for Indian textile players.
exam_angle: India's textile sector is a major employment generator and export earner; Bharat Tex is a flagship government initiative relevant to GS-3 industrial policy and GS-2 government schemes.
key_facts: Event: Bharat Tex 2026, India's largest global textile event
Inaugurated by: Union Minister of Textiles
Record international participation at the 2026 edition
Context: India aims to become a global textile manufacturing hub under PM MITRA scheme

title: India at 49th Session of Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC49): Strengthening Food Safety Leadership
summary: India participated and strengthened its leadership role at the 49th Session of the Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC49), which sets international food safety and quality standards. The Codex Alimentarius Commission is a joint body of FAO and WHO. India's active participation is significant for its agricultural exports, as Codex standards are referenced in WTO's SPS (Sanitary and Phytosanitary) Agreement.
exam_angle: Codex Alimentarius Commission, its parent bodies (FAO/WHO), and its role in WTO's SPS Agreement are standard exam questions under international organisations and food security.
key_facts: Event: 49th Session of Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC49)
Codex Alimentarius Commission: joint FAO-WHO body for international food standards
Standards are referenced in WTO's SPS Agreement
India's participation strengthens position as an agricultural exporter

title: Indian-Origin NASA Astronaut Anil Menon Travels to International Space Station
summary: Indian-origin NASA astronaut Colonel Anil Menon has blasted off on his maiden trip to the International Space Station (ISS) aboard a Soyuz spacecraft. Anil Menon, born to immigrant parents from Kerala and Russia, is a flight surgeon and was selected as a NASA astronaut in 2021. He is part of the broader context of Indian-origin representation in global space exploration.
exam_angle: Indian-origin persons in significant global scientific roles are relevant for 'Persons in News'; Soyuz spacecraft and ISS are standard sci-tech facts for UPSC.
key_facts: Astronaut: Col. Anil Menon, Indian-origin NASA astronaut
Mission: Maiden trip to International Space Station (ISS)
Vehicle: Soyuz spacecraft
Menon was selected as NASA astronaut in 2021; parents have Kerala-Russian roots

title: Supreme Court Pulls Up Patna High Court Over 'Grabbing Breast Not Rape Attempt' Order
summary: The Supreme Court of India pulled up the Patna High Court for its controversial ruling that 'grabbing a breast does not constitute an attempt to rape.' The Supreme Court expressed strong disapproval of such judicial reasoning, emphasising that such orders reflect a narrow and legally incorrect interpretation of sexual offences under the Indian Penal Code/Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The matter is now under judicial scrutiny at the apex court level.
exam_angle: Judicial interpretation of sexual offence laws, the role of the Supreme Court in correcting High Court judgements, and the legal definition of 'attempt to rape' under Indian criminal law are important polity/governance exam topics.
key_facts: Supreme Court pulled up Patna High Court for ruling on sexual offence
HC had ruled 'grabbing breast does not constitute attempt to rape'
SC emphasised correct legal interpretation of sexual offence provisions
Relevant law: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) / IPC provisions on sexual assault

title: AI171 Ahmedabad Plane Crash: AAIB Tells Supreme Court Draft Final Report Expected in October 2026
summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) informed the Supreme Court of India that the draft final investigation report into the Air India Flight AI171 Ahmedabad plane crash is likely to be completed by October 2026. The crash, involving an Air India aircraft, was one of the deadliest aviation accidents in recent Indian history. The Supreme Court is monitoring the investigation's progress.
exam_angle: The AAIB (Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau) and its role under the Aircraft Act, aviation safety regulation by DGCA, and Supreme Court's role in monitoring public safety investigations are important institutional knowledge points.
key_facts: Investigating body: AAIB (Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau), under MoCA
Flight: Air India AI171, Ahmedabad crash
Draft final report expected: October 2026 (as told to Supreme Court)
DGCA regulates civil aviation in India; AAIB investigates accidents independently

title: India Responds to US Indictment of Lawrence Bishnoi Gang; Reaffirms Anti-Terror Cooperation
summary: India's MEA issued its first formal response to the US Department of Justice indictment of members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang in connection with a murder in Canada, reaffirming India's commitment to combating organised crime and terrorism. The MEA stated that Indo-US cooperation on countering organised crime is 'strong.' The case is linked to the broader India-Canada diplomatic tensions over allegations of Indian state involvement in killings of Sikh separatists on Canadian soil.
exam_angle: The Lawrence Bishnoi gang case connects India-Canada diplomatic tensions, India-US counterterrorism cooperation, and transnational organised crime — all key GS-2 topics.
key_facts: US DoJ indicted Lawrence Bishnoi gang members over murder in Canada
India's MEA reaffirmed commitment to fighting organised crime and terrorism
Indo-US cooperation on organised crime described as 'strong' by MEA
Case connected to broader India-Canada tensions over Sikh separatist killings

title: Sonam Wangchuk's Hunger Strike Enters Day 17; Loses 8.5 kg Over Ladakh Demands
summary: Climate activist and engineer Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike entered its 17th day, during which he has lost 8.5 kg. Wangchuk is demanding full statehood for Ladakh, inclusion of Ladakh in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution (to protect tribal land rights), a public service commission for Ladakh, and parliamentary representation. His strike has drawn national attention and calls from public figures urging him to end the fast.
exam_angle: The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution (tribal autonomy in NE India and its possible extension to Ladakh), Ladakh's UT status post Article 370 abrogation, and demands for statehood are critical polity topics.
key_facts: Sonam Wangchuk on Day 17 of hunger strike; lost 8.5 kg
Key demands: Statehood for Ladakh, inclusion in Sixth Schedule, Ladakh PSC
Ladakh became a UT (without legislature) after Article 370 abrogation in August 2019
Sixth Schedule currently covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram

title: Dholera International Airport Progress Reviewed by Civil Aviation Minister
summary: Union Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu reviewed the progress of the Dholera International Airport in Gujarat, describing it as a 'key catalyst for India's future-ready economic growth.' Dholera is part of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC) and is being developed as India's first greenfield smart city. The airport is expected to serve the Dholera Special Investment Region (DSIR).
exam_angle: Dholera Smart City, DMIC (Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor), and greenfield airports under UDAN/NABH Nirman scheme are important infrastructure topics for GS-3.
key_facts: Airport: Dholera International Airport, Gujarat
Reviewed by: Union Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu
Dholera is India's first greenfield smart city under DMIC project
Located in Dholera Special Investment Region (DSIR)

title: India-US Defence Technology Partnership: Ambitious Agenda, Limited Delivery
summary: An analysis highlights that despite high-level commitments under the India-US defence partnership — including the iCET (Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology) framework and the Defence Technology and Trade Initiative (DTTI) — actual technology transfer and co-production outcomes have remained limited. Key pending areas include GE-414 jet engine co-production, armed drones (MQ-9B Predator), and advanced semiconductor collaboration.
exam_angle: iCET, DTTI, and US-India defence technology cooperation are standard topics in India's defence and foreign policy; the gap between stated ambition and delivery is a critical analytical point for GS-2 Mains essays.
key_facts: Framework: iCET (Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology) — launched 2023
Defence Technology and Trade Initiative (DTTI) is the older bilateral defence tech body
Pending deals: GE-414 jet engine co-production, MQ-9B Predator drones
Criticism: limited actual technology transfer despite high-level commitments

title: BITS Pilani Tops Hurun India Under-30 Entrepreneurship List; IIT Delhi Second
summary: BITS Pilani has topped the Hurun India Under-30 list, producing the highest number of young entrepreneurs, followed by IIT Delhi. The Hurun India U30 report tracks the alma maters of India's most successful entrepreneurs under 30 years of age. The report highlights the growing startup ecosystem from premier technical institutions.
exam_angle: Rankings and reports on India's innovation/startup ecosystem, the role of IITs/NITs in entrepreneurship, and government initiatives like Startup India are relevant for GS-3.
key_facts: Report: Hurun India Under-30 list
Top institution: BITS Pilani (highest number of young entrepreneurs)
Second: IIT Delhi
Reflects India's growing startup and innovation ecosystem

title: Graham Staines Murder Case: Supreme Court Directs Odisha to Decide on Dara Singh's Release Within a Month
summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Odisha government to decide within one month on the release application of Dara Singh, the prime convict in the 1999 Graham Staines murder case. Graham Staines, an Australian Christian missionary, and his two minor sons were burnt alive in Keonjhar district of Odisha by a mob led by Dara Singh. Dara Singh was awarded life imprisonment by the Supreme Court in 2011.
exam_angle: The Graham Staines case is a landmark case on communal violence, freedom of religion (Article 25), and the Supreme Court's power over remission of sentences; relevant for both polity and ethics papers.
key_facts: Case: Graham Staines murder, 1999 — Keonjhar, Odisha
Victim: Australian missionary Graham Staines and his two minor sons, burnt alive
Convict: Dara Singh, awarded life imprisonment by SC in 2011
SC directed Odisha to decide on Dara Singh's release application within one month
